Approval of April 17, 2024, Minutes
Chair Saleh called for a motion to approve the minutes. Motion to approve by Viviana
Gomez, seconded by Karina Macias. The initial vote did not pass due to abstentions from
members who were not present at the last meeting. After clarification, a second roll call
was conducted. Votes to approve: Bell, Bell Gardens, Huntington Park, South Gate, LA
County. Abstentions: Cerritos. Minutes approved.

 2. Update by Staff
The COG has selected Eric Shen as the technical liaison between Metro and the cities
for the SGL project. He will be working very closely with the cities to help address any
questions or challenges you may have.
Advocacy in Sacramento and State Budget
Members of the committee completed two advocacy trips to Sacramento in May. On
behalf of Hector, we thank all members who were able to attend. We also acknowledge
Supervisor Hahn and Metro 1st Vice Chair Fernando Dutra for their participation and
support.
Planned September Trip to Washington DC
Tentatively looking at September 15-17, 2024 for an advocacy trip to Washington DC.
Our next step would be to secure funding for the project in the next federal fiscal year
budget. The plan is to meet with our U.S. Senators, Congressional delegation, and staff
at the U.S. Department of Transportation. Once we have confirmed this date, we will send
out more details to committee members.
Support Letter for $500 Million for TIRCP Cycle 7
Metro requested city support letters for a $500 million state grant application for the
Southeast Gateway Line. The funds will be used to leverage a New Starts award from the
Federal Transit Administration. All corridor cities have submitted their support letters by
Thursday, July 18.
Youth Video Competition
The COG is preparing to launch a video competition for middle school, high school and
community college students who live in the communities along the SGL alignment.
The purpose of the video competition is to elevate community engagement and
awareness for the Southeast Gateway Line through a cutting-edge social media
campaign, an interactive video competition, and strategic school outreach. We will be
inviting students to participate from schools within LA Unified, Montebello, Lynwood,
Downey, Paramount, Norwalk/La Mirada, Bellflower, and ABC Unified, as well as East LA
College and Cerritos College. We will be launching this when students return to school in
the Fall and will offer scholarship awards to the winners. This was funded from a transfer

 of funds from the former Eco-Rapid Transit to the COG. Staff will send out more details
and will seek Committee members to promote the contest with your residents and youth.
3. Southeast Gateway Line Corridor Cities Committee Update by Metro
Due to the absence of Metro staff, Eric Shen reported that a recent update by Metro staff
at the SGL City Managers TAC Meeting on the 3% calculation and eligible project lists.
Detailed report to follow in future meetings.
4. Update on the SGL Public-Private Partnership (P3) Assessment
Metro staff has requested to postpone this item to the next meeting. Ms. Gomez briefly
outlined the assessment findings, which P3 model not suitable for this project due to low
value for money cost savings.
5. Action Item: Approve Annual Committee Membership Dues – $10,000 per
  member agency for FY2024/25
Eric Shen presented the staff recommendation on the annual dues and explained how
the dues will be used. Chair Saleh and committee members raised concerns about the
timing in relations to each city’s budget adoption process. The Committee decided to
postpone the approval so each member could consult with their city managers.
6. New Business/Items for Discussion: None

7. Remaining Schedule for 2024: September 18 and November 20, 2024 at 6pm
  Pacific Time. Eric noted that the September meeting may be rescheduled due to the
  DC advocacy trip.
Adjournment: The meeting was adjourned at 6:51 pm Pacific Time.

1. July 17, 2024, Minutes
Quorum was not reached. Minutes for prior SGL CCC meeting on July 17, 2024 were not
approved and will be considered at next meeting.
2. Update by Staff
Gateway Cities COG Executive Director Hector De La Torre provided the update by staff.
SGL CCC 20241120 DRAFT MINUTES
Page 1 of 4
 FTA Record of Decision for SGL
The Southeast Gateway Line project received a Record of Decision (ROD) from the
Federal Transit Administration in August 2024, which allows the project to be eligible for
future federal funding. August also saw the completion and submission of the federal New
Starts rating activities for the SGL project for FTA review.
Nearby/Regional Transit Projects
October 2024 saw the Foothill Gold Line Construction Authority sign a $798 million
agreement with Metro to complete construction of the A Line extension to Montclair in
San Bernardino County. A recent update on the Inglewood People Mover project shows
its status as increasingly uncertain. The SGL project continues to be the highest priority
Metro project in LA County.
SGL Funding/Milestones
October 2024 saw Metro receive $231 million in state TIRCP Cycle 7 funds for the SGL
project. GCCOG staff connected Metro staff with CARB staff to write a successful TIRCP
grant application.
SGL utility relocation groundbreaking was held in Artesia in October 2024.
Youth Video Competition
GCCOG will be hosting a 3-minute youth film competition called Southeast LA Youth
Filmmakers Festival all about “SELA Stories” or films that capture the SELA of today and
students’ visions for tomorrow. There will be $5,000 in college scholarship prizes as well
as non-monetary prizes. Films are due Dec 1, 2024 and winners will be announced Dec.
9, 2024. www.selastories.com
SGL 3% Contribution/Other Metro Updates
This year and into next we will continue discussion at SGL City Managers TAC of in-kind
contributions and other options to satisfy SGL 3% contribution for relevant jurisdictions.
Metro staff to present Slauson/A Line to LA Union Station study findings to Metro Board
in next few months.
Metro plans to award ROW consultant contract and request to enter into project
engineering agreement with FTA by January 2025.

SGL CCC 20241120 DRAFT MINUTES
Page 2 of 4
 State Advocacy/State Budget Update
Late January 2025 (after budget) there will be a SGL advocacy trip to Sacramento.
Current state revenue appears to be running ahead of projections, particularly because
of income tax revenue going up with a strong stock market. With recent 2024 cuts, the
state’s projected budget for next year appears to be roughly balanced. Likely there will be
no additional spending but this is a good sign for cities and SGL because California is in
a (somewhat reduced but) normal budget. We do not expect to see the previously
projected $30 billion in cuts from last spring.
3. Southeast Gateway Line Corridor Cities Committee Update by Metro
  Metro staff June Susilo reported that Hector’s Update from Staff was very
  comprehensive. She added that her team at Metro continues to advance engineering
  and design to get the high-risk items out of the way, beginning with utility relocation,
  then soil abatement, freight relocation, and light rail construction. Metro is meeting
  regularly and coordinating with city staff to advance those design components, looking
  to award a CMGC contractor who will come on board in spring 2025 (for pre-
  construction activities).
4. Metro Government Relations Update: Metro government relations staff had a
  scheduling conflict and were unable to attend. GCCOG staff Marisa Perez provided a
  brief federal update about recent discussion of how the SGL project agenda should
  be presented during the new administration. She noted that Metro has been
  successful in past Trump administrations [ex. Funding for Metro D Line (Purple)].
  Hector De La Torre conveyed that SGL CCC will have to advocate strongly through
  bipartisan organizations like National League of Cities, US Mayors Conference, and
  other national orgs of city/elected officials for the next four years. Marisa discussed
  forming coalitions with transit advocates in red states to make sure our projects keep
  moving forward. Hector discussed how the construction of Metro’s light rail train cars
  will likely be in Alabama and to advocate accordingly.
5. 2025 Advocacy Trip Dates: GCCOG staff to send out Doodle poll to SGL CCC
  members to identify dates that work for upcoming late January/early February 2025
  SGL advocacy trip to Sacramento. Proposed budget for CA Governor comes out Jan
  10 and Hector De La Torre suggested early February due to typical travel behavior of
  state legislators.

6. New Business/Items for Discussion: None
